blocks.text: Home Affairs orders rapid review of government-wide cyber systems after OpenAI hack
OpenAI’s Medicare breach has prompted a government-wide assessment of cyber systems to bolster Australia’s public sector against further AI threats – deliberate or not.

Home affairs directed all government departments and agencies to undertake a “rapid” stocktake of legacy systems, to formulate risk management for legacy technology and to report their compliance back to the department.
The directive prioritises systems of government significance – the government’s critical systems – with a review due by the end of the year, while other systems will be assessed by March.
The acting home affairs minister, Richard Marles, said AI is “changing the environment in which we operate at extraordinary speed.”
double quotation markWe can’t wait for an old system to fail before replacing it. We need to identify vulnerabilities and deal with them before they can be exploited.

blocks.text: Albanese to announce next stage of Melbourne airport rail link
Benita Kolovos

Early works are beginning on the second stage of the long-awaited train line to Melbourne Airport – a 7.6km stretch of the train line from Albion, in Sunshine West, to Keilor East, where a new station will be built.
Anthony Albanese will be in Melbourne today with Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, to announce that site investigations, procurement and development work will begin in the coming weeks.
Built alongside the Jacana freight corridor, this stage of the project will feature a 500m rail bridge to carry trains over the Maribyrnong River.
Community engagement and early designs will follow next year, with major construction to begin in 2028 and finish in 2031.
The first stage of Melbourne Airport Rail, which involves the creation of the “Sunshine superhub” and the construction of new stations at Tottenham and Albion, is expected to be completed in 2030.
A man has been charged with murder after the deaths of two men at Gurranang, about 25km north of Grafton in northern New South Wales, police said.
About 3pm on Sunday 13 September, police were called to a house following reports the body of a 79-year-old man had been found.
Officers visited the house again on Monday when they found the body of a 59-year-old man in a shed on the property.
Detectives arrested a 32-year-old man at a hospital in Grafton yesterday afternoon.
He was taken to Grafton police station where he was charged with two counts of murder and stealing a motor vehicle.
He was refused bail to appear before court today.
